title: Trent Session 4 — equal piety for unwritten traditions restricted to first two kinds
source_text: XV. Itaque ad duo tantum priora traditionum genera restringunt Decretum Concilii Tridentini, quod habetur Sessione quarta: ubi praecipitur ut traditiones non scriptae pari pietatis affectu suscipiantur atque ipsi libri Scripturae Canonicae. Verba Concilii sunt, Synodus perspiciens Evangelii veritatem & disciplinam contineri in libris scriptis, & sine scripto traditionibus, quae ipsius Christi ore ab Apostolis acceptae, aut ab ipsis Apostolis Spiritu sancto dictante, quasi per manus traditae, ad nos usque pervenerunt, Orthodoxorum Patrum exempla secuta, omnes libros tam Veteris quam Novi Testamenti, cum utriusque unus Deus sit author, necnon traditiones ipsas tum ad fidem, tum ad mores pertinentes, tanquam, vel ore tenus a Christo, vel a Spiritu sancto dictatas, & continua successione in Ecclesia Catholica conservatas, pari pietatis affectu & reverentia suscipit & veneratur.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore they restrict the Decree of the Council of Trent, which is found in Session four — where it is commanded that unwritten traditions be received with equal affection of piety as the Canonical books of Scripture themselves — to the two prior kinds of traditions only. The words of the Council are: The Synod, seeing that the truth and discipline of the Gospel are contained in written books and in unwritten traditions, which, received from Christ's own mouth by the Apostles, or handed on from the Apostles themselves as the Holy Spirit dictated, as if by hand, have come down to us — following the examples of the orthodox Fathers — receives and venerates with equal affection of piety and reverence all the books of both the Old and New Testament, since one God is the author of both, and also those traditions pertaining to faith and to morals, as dictated either orally by Christ or by the Holy Spirit, and conserved by continual succession in the Catholic Church.
pass_b_english: They therefore confine Trent's Session 4 rule — receive unwritten traditions with the same piety as the Canonical books — to the first two kinds alone (Divine and Apostolic).

The Council says: seeing Gospel truth and discipline live in written books and in unwritten traditions received from Christ's mouth by the Apostles, or passed from the Apostles under the Spirit's dictation as if by hand down to us, the Synod, following the orthodox Fathers, receives and venerates with equal piety and reverence every Old and New Testament book (one God their author) and those faith-and-morals traditions spoken by Christ or the Spirit and kept by continual succession in the Catholic Church.

choices.why: Roman doctors limit Trent's equal-piety rule to Divine/Apostolic only, not Ecclesiastical.
Trent's exact equal-reception formula; keep close.
